floor_history.headline: Recon s1: floor re-measured 32 (chassis unchanged, all WIP-imported verdicts spendable); $v0/$v1 exchange confirmed at .greg disposition level (pseudo 100 in $v1, 83/84/98 in $v0); frontier = instrume

Structural respelling dropped the honest floor 32 -> 14 and RETRACTS the s1 'RA exchange validated unreachable' verdict: every $v0/$v1 hunk inverse.py had foreclosed closed under ordinary shared-named

frontier.hypothesis: Residual (2) - the arm synth-mult chain in $v0 instead of $v1, worth ~10 of the remaining 14 - is reachable by an HONEST C shape that raises the destination pseudo's allocno priority without chain-extension.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc gives the synth-mult chain temp its own quantity unless the destination pseudo's priority is high enough for combine/regmove to tie them; reg_n_refs (write count) is the measured control knob, but read count and live-range length feed the same priority.
frontier.next_probe: Look for a formulation where the arm value is genuinely READ more than once or lives longer - e.g. the interpolation expressed so the arm result feeds two consumers, or the `use_high` branch restructured so the value crosses the join with a second use. Do NOT re-derive the 5-write decomposition (banked, policy-blocked until the ladder is spent). Dump-check with tools/grinder/dump.ps1 and read .lreg/.greg for the chain temp's quantity.

frontier.hypothesis: Residual (1), the 2-insn `sh zero,0(gp)` placement (ours 64, target 56), is a pure scheduler-priority question with no source-level handle.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 sched.c list-scheduler priority for a dependence-free store in the early-exit block; measured NOT controllable by statement position (9 slots swept) or by split-init interleaving.
frontier.next_probe: tools/sched_solver (models sched.c exactly, 6978/6978 per the sched-solver-campaign-2026-08-05 memory) on the early-exit basic block: ask what input change moves the store 8 slots earlier. Forensics modality.

frontier.hypothesis: Residual (3), the tail `lw`/`sra` swap plus the missing load-delay nop, is the same scheduler question as residual (1) and is likely coupled to residual (2) since both live in the post-join block.
frontier.mechanism: The load's INSN_PRIORITY exceeds the sra's due to MIPS load latency; target's build ranked them the other way, eats a maspsx nop, and therefore has 231 insns to our 230.
frontier.next_probe: Same sched_solver run as residual (1), applied to the post-join block; and re-diff the tail immediately after any residual-(2) win, since an allocation change there may flip the ready-list ranking for free.
